title: 四级主题练习 03 · 研究与沟通
description: 原创缩编练习，学习情境为虚构，覆盖非听力题型。主题参考：学生研究、求职沟通与日常习惯。

sections.title: 写作
sections.instructions: 按题目要求完成写作。提交后查看参考范文，自行核对。
study_paragraphs: A small research project can help students improve campus services by replacing guesses with evidence. For example, a team could study why the bicycle parking area near the library is often crowded. They could count bicycles at different times, interview users and draw a map of the available spaces. These methods would reveal whether the problem came from too few spaces, unclear signs or abandoned bicycles. The students should protect people's privacy and avoid collecting information they do not need. After examining the results, they could recommend one affordable change and test it for a week. The project would teach them to ask clear questions, cooperate and evaluate an idea. It would also show that useful research does not always require expensive equipment. Careful observation can be a good starting point.

questions.prompt: Write 120–180 words explaining how a small research project could improve one campus service. Use an example of your own.

sections.title: 选词填空
sections.instructions: 从词库选词，每词只用一次。
paragraphs: A student team wanted to improve an online appointment service. They began by [1] ______ how visitors used it. Their first [2] ______ was that the buttons were too small, but interviews suggested a different problem. The available times were not [3] ______ explained. The team tested a new page and asked users for [4] ______. They decided to keep collecting evidence before reaching a final [5] ______.
study_paragraphs: A student team wanted to improve an online appointment service. They began by observing how visitors used it. Their first assumption was that the buttons were too small, but interviews suggested a different problem. The available times were not clearly explained. The team tested a new page and asked users for feedback. They decided to keep collecting evidence before reaching a final conclusion.

questions.explanation: 第 1 空填入 observing，结合上下文和句法关系判断。
第 2 空填入 assumption，结合上下文和句法关系判断。
第 3 空填入 clearly，结合上下文和句法关系判断。
第 4 空填入 feedback，结合上下文和句法关系判断。
第 5 空填入 conclusion，结合上下文和句法关系判断。

sections.title: 信息匹配 · 面试准备
sections.instructions: 根据段落内容完成匹配。
paragraphs: [A] Before a video interview, Jo practised explaining one project to a friend. The friend interrupted whenever a term was unclear. Jo then replaced unnecessary technical words with concrete examples. This helped her describe her work to someone outside her course.

[B] Sam placed a short list of questions beside his screen. He wanted to understand how interns would receive training and feedback. The list prevented him from forgetting what mattered when the conversation became busy. He still listened rather than reading the questions mechanically.

[C] The interviewer offered Anika a chance to begin again after the connection failed. Anika briefly explained what had happened and repeated only the part that had been lost. A calm explanation was more useful than apologising throughout the rest of the meeting.

[D] After the interview, Ben wrote down a question that had been difficult to answer. He checked his project records and prepared a clearer example for next time. He did not assume that one uncomfortable answer proved he was unsuited to the whole field.

sections.title: 阅读理解 · The study behind the survey
sections.instructions: 阅读短文，选择最合适的答案。
paragraphs: A campus café wanted to know whether students preferred a longer menu. The manager placed a survey beside the counter at noon. Most respondents asked for more hot meals. The manager almost ordered a new cooking unit, but a student researcher noticed that the survey had reached mainly lunch customers.

The researcher returned in the morning and evening. Early visitors cared about quick service, while later visitors wanted a quiet place to study. The café tested different arrangements at different times instead of extending the menu all day. The first survey had not been useless; it had answered a narrower question than the manager originally thought. Knowing who supplied the evidence changed how that evidence could be used.

questions.prompt: What was the limitation of the first survey?

options.text: It asked about an unrelated building.
It was completed only by staff.
It included no questions about food.

questions.explanation: 调查只在中午开展，样本偏向午餐顾客。

questions.prompt: What did the café eventually try?

options.text: A cooking unit for every table.

questions.explanation: 后续结果显示不同时段需求不同，因此分时测试。

questions.prompt: What lesson does the passage offer?

options.text: The source of evidence affects its interpretation.

questions.explanation: 调查对象决定了证据可以支持什么结论。

sections.title: 阅读理解 · A pause before the reply
sections.instructions: 阅读短文，选择最合适的答案。
paragraphs: During a group meeting, a message from an absent member appeared on the screen: the latest plan was "not ready". Rui felt that his work had been dismissed and immediately began writing an angry reply. Before sending it, he asked another member to read the message with him.

They noticed that the message also requested missing cost figures. Rui asked which figures were needed and learned that the absent member was preparing a funding application. The plan had not been rejected; it needed information for a different purpose. Rui kept a simple rule after that meeting: when a short message seems hostile, clarify its meaning before deciding how to respond. The rule did not guarantee agreement, but it prevented some avoidable arguments.

questions.prompt: Why were the cost figures requested?
questions.explanation: 对方正在准备资金申请，需要费用信息。

questions.prompt: What does Rui's later rule recommend?
questions.explanation: 短消息看似不友好时，先核对其含义。

sections.title: 翻译 · 中译英
sections.instructions: 完成翻译，提交后查看参考译文。
paragraphs: 一些大学正在鼓励学生参加社区调查。学生先与居民交谈，了解他们在生活中遇到的困难，再把观察结果整理成报告。通过这样的实践，学生能够学习如何提出问题、收集证据并尊重不同意见。他们的建议也可能为社区服务的改进提供帮助。
study_paragraphs: Some universities are encouraging students to conduct community surveys. Students first talk with residents about difficulties in their daily lives and then organise their observations into reports. Through this practice, students can learn to ask questions, gather evidence and respect different opinions. Their suggestions may also help improve community services.
